title: Coefficient-linear derived projection from a specified ordinary slice comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small Grothendieck site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $V\in\mathcal C$, and $R\to S$ a unital map of commutative ring sheaves. Use the slice rings $R_V=R|_V$, $S_V=S|_V$, module sheaves, sheaf tensor, and ordinary unbounded derived categories with localizations $Q$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $j_{R!},j_{S!}$ be the exact slice extensions [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Use derived extension of scalars as pullback for the identity underlying topos, with its canonical K-flat computation counits [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], and exact scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-weil-pbc-restriction-derived-products]. Suppose given natural isomorphisms
$$\kappa_N:\operatorname{Res}j_{S!}N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{R!}\operatorname{Res}N,\qquad \eta_M:j_{R!}M\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{S!}(M\otimes_{R_V}S_V),$$
with $\eta_M$ $S$-linear and $\kappa$ the identity on the direct-sum extension generators [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. Write $r_P$ for the underlying $R$-linear cochain isomorphism obtained by applying $\kappa\eta$ to each term of a complex $P$.
There is a unique natural $S$-linear derived isomorphism
$$\beta_K:(j_{R!}K)\otimes_R^LS\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{S!}(K\otimes_{R_V}^LS_V),\qquad K\in D(R_V),$$
whose value on every flat-term K-flat complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] is localization of the degreewise $\eta_P$ conjugated by the specified scalar-extension counits and exact-extension comparisons. Its scalar restriction, followed by derived $\kappa$, is precisely the unique natural $R$-linear comparison normalized by $Q(r_P)$ and the one-sided tensor comparisons [lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization]. In particular any natural $R$-linear comparison with that same representative equation equals the scalar restriction of $\beta$; this applies to evaluation of a derived strict-tower comparison whenever its computation comparisons have the indicated normalization. The statement holds without flatness of $R\to S$, boundedness or completeness.

proof.text: Work in homotopy categories and put $\mathcal P=\mathcal P_{R_V}$, the full subcategory of flat-term K-flat complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] its localization at quasi-isomorphisms is equivalent to $D(R_V)$. Write $J_R,J_S$ for the derived exact extensions and $E,E_V$ for the specified derived changes of rings on the ambient and slice sites. Exactness in [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives natural comparisons $\phi^R_C:J_RQ_{R_V}C\cong Q_Rj_{R!}C$ and $\phi^S_D:J_SQ_{S_V}D\cong Q_Sj_{S!}D$ for arbitrary complexes. By [lem-cbc-ringed-open-flat-resolution], $j_{R!}P$ is K-flat with flat terms for every $P\in\mathcal P$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] makes both $\epsilon_{j_{R!}P}$ and $\epsilon^V_P$ invertible. All four sites here are the original small site or its small slice; every coefficient category is the ordinary module-sheaf category.

Apply the given natural $S$-linear $\eta$ degreewise to $P$. It gives a chain isomorphism $h_P:j_{R!}P\otimes_RS\cong j_{S!}(P\otimes_{R_V}S_V)$. Indeed the differential square is exactly naturality of $\eta$ for $d^i:P^i\to P^{i+1}$. For a chain map $f:P\to P'$ the same naturality gives $h_{P'}(j_{R!}f\otimes1)=j_{S!}(f\otimes1)h_P$. This equation also holds for a chain homotopy, degree by degree: the two functors are additive, and applying them to $f-g=dh+hd$ gives that same identity after applying either functor. Hence $Q_Sh_P$ is natural on the full homotopy subcategory $\mathcal P$. This is a use of the specified $\eta$, not a replacement by an unspecified projection isomorphism.

source.place: Degreewise application of the supplied ordinary comparison; elementary naturality calculation

proof.text:
Set $F=EJ_R$ and $G=J_SE_V$. For $P\in\mathcal P$ define the following isomorphisms, with composition written right to left:
$$a_P=\epsilon_{j_{R!}P}\,E(\phi^R_P):F(Q_{R_V}P)\longrightarrow Q_S(j_{R!}P\otimes_RS),$$
$$b_P=\phi^S_{P\otimes S_V}\,J_S(\epsilon^V_P):G(Q_{R_V}P)\longrightarrow Q_Sj_{S!}(P\otimes_{R_V}S_V).$$
Here the counit $\epsilon$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] has target $Q_S(S\otimes_R j_{R!}P)$, and its target is written $Q_S(j_{R!}P\otimes_RS)$ through the degreewise symmetry of the sheaf tensor with a degree-zero factor (no sign), the order in which $\eta$ is given; likewise on the slice. Their naturality on $\mathcal P$ follows from the natural transformations in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Consequently $t_P=b_P^{-1}Q_S(h_P)a_P$ is a natural isomorphism between the restrictions of $F$ and $G$ to $\mathcal P$. These are morphisms in $D(S)$ throughout; in particular the coefficient action is retained before any scalar restriction.

proof.text: Use the equivalence $W^{-1}\mathcal P\simeq D(R_V)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and the transformation part of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. The functors $FQ|_{\mathcal P}$ and $GQ|_{\mathcal P}$ invert $W$ because $Q$ does. Their natural isomorphism $t$ therefore extends uniquely to $\beta:F\cong G$ with $\beta_{QP}=t_P$. To see the independence and naturality explicitly, naturality for $w:P\to P'$ in $W$ also gives naturality for $(Qw)^{-1}$ by multiplying its naturality equation by the two inverse isomorphisms; composition gives it for every localized morphism. Transport across the displayed equivalence gives naturality for every morphism of $D(R_V)$. The same procedure applied to $t^{-1}$ gives the inverse of $\beta$. Any competing normalized transformation restricts to $t$ and hence equals $\beta$.

proof.text:
Write $U:D(S)\to D(R)$ and $U_V:D(S_V)\to D(R_V)$ for exact scalar restriction, using [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-derived-products]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the given $\kappa$ gives a natural isomorphism $k:UJ_S\cong J_RU_V$ whose representative is $Q_R\kappa$. Let $A(K)=J_RK\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S[0]$ and $B(K)=J_R(K\otimes_{R_V}^{\mathbf L}S_V[0])$, with rings on the tensor right regarded as restricted modules. The right-sided comparisons of [lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization] give
$$A_P:A(QP)\cong Q_R(j_{R!}P\otimes_RS),\qquad B_P:B(QP)\cong Q_Rj_{R!}(P\otimes_{R_V}S_V).$$
For $A_P$ insert $\phi^R_P$ then the comparison with K-flat left factor $j_{R!}P$; for $B_P$ apply $J_R$ to the comparison with K-flat left factor $P$ then insert $\phi^R_{P\otimes S_V}$. They are natural on $\mathcal P$ even though $S[0]$ and $S_V[0]$ can be nonflat. The underlying ordinary scalar-extension tensors are the same tensors in these formulas, by [lem-cbc-extension-tensor-comparison-independent] (using the symmetry to put $S$ on the right).

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and preceding construction), Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); exact scalar restriction and ordinary scalar tensor identification

proof.text:
On $\mathcal P$ the identity of the preceding ordinary tensor models defines isomorphisms $x_P:UF(QP)\to A(QP)$ by $A_P^{-1}U(a_P)$ and $y_P:J_RU_VE_V(QP)\to B(QP)$ by
$$B_P^{-1}Q_R(\kappa_{P\otimes S_V})\,U(b_P)\,k_{E_V(QP)}^{-1}.$$
The exact-restriction comparisons are inserted in these formulas. Each is natural, so [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] extend them uniquely to natural isomorphisms $x:UF\cong A$ and $y:J_RU_VE_V\cong B$. These are precisely the scalar-to-tensor identifications normalized by the specified counits and the one-sided comparisons. For $y$ this is not built in by the factors $\kappa$ and $k^{-1}$: naturality of $k$ along $\epsilon^V_P:E_V(QP)\cong Q_{S_V}(P\otimes S_V)$ and the representative $Q_R\kappa$ of $k$ (Step 5) give $Q_R(\kappa_{P\otimes S_V})U(b_P)k^{-1}_{E_V(QP)}=\phi^R_{P\otimes S_V}J_R(U_V\epsilon^V_P)$, the exact-restriction comparisons inserted, so $y$ is $J_R$ of the slice identification $U_VE_V\cong-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_V}S_V[0]$ defined like $x$; hence $\rho$ below is not normalized by its own definition. Substitute the formulas for $x,y$ and $\beta_{QP}=b_P^{-1}Q_Sh_Pa_P$ in $\rho=y\,k_{E_V}\,U(\beta)\,x^{-1}$. Adjacent inverse factors cancel, leaving
$$B_P\,\rho_{QP}=Q_R(\kappa_{P\otimes S_V}h_P)A_P=Q_R(r_P)A_P.$$
The final equality is the definition of $r_P$ in the item. This checks the claimed representative equation without using faithfulness of derived scalar restriction.

source.place: Tags 06YU and 06YY: representative-normalized scalar restriction; categories.tex Tags 04VG and 04VK: natural transformation descent

proof.text: If $\rho':A\to B$ is any natural $R$-linear comparison with $B_P\rho'_{QP}=Q_R(r_P)A_P$, Step 6 gives $\rho'_{QP}=\rho_{QP}$ for all $P\in\mathcal P$. The same resolving localization and its fully faithful restriction on transformations [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent, lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] imply $\rho'=\rho$. In particular, once a strict-tower evaluation has the stated source and target computations and representative equation, this uniqueness applies to it directly. No statement about evaluation computing a derived functor is assumed without that normalization hypothesis. The argument used only flatness of the chosen resolving terms, never flatness of $R\to S$, boundedness of a complex, or completion.
